title: Natural positive-degree Roos computation for abelian towers
statement: Let Ab(N) be the category of countable inverse systems of abelian groups [def-weil-inverse-system], with enough injectives [def-sp-enough-injectives], and let lim be its additive inverse-limit functor [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. For each tower A=(A_n,f_n:A_(n+1)→A_n), define t_A on the product by t_A(x)_n=x_n-f_n(x_(n+1)) [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism]. There are simultaneous isomorphisms e_A:R¹lim A ≅ coker(t_A), natural in every morphism of towers: the componentwise product map commutes with t and e identifies its induced cokernel map with R¹lim of the morphism. For every q≥2 and every A, R^q lim A is zero. No kernel or left-exactness conclusion is part of this statement.

source.place: Tag 07KW (More on Algebra, Lemma 15.88.1), computation of Rlim by the two-term Roos complex

proof.text: Construction (Stacks 07KW, proof). For the tower $(A_n,f_n)_{n\geq1}$ let $B_n=A_n\oplus A_{n-1}\oplus\cdots\oplus A_1$ and $C_n=A_{n-1}\oplus\cdots\oplus A_1$ ($C_1=0$), both with the projections forgetting the first summand as transition maps $B_{n+1}\to B_n$, $C_{n+1}\to C_n$; these transition maps are surjective. Let $A_n\to B_n$ be $a\mapsto(a,f_{n-1}(a),f_{n-2}f_{n-1}(a),\dots,f_1\cdots f_{n-1}(a))$ and $B_n\to C_n$ be $(x_n,\dots,x_1)\mapsto(x_i-f_i(x_{i+1}))_{1\leq i\leq n-1}$; both commute with the transition maps, so they are morphisms of inverse systems [def-weil-inverse-system]. For each $n$ the sequence $0\to A_n\to B_n\to C_n\to0$ is exact: the first map is injective (first coordinate), the kernel of the second is the set of $(x_i)$ with $x_i=f_i(x_{i+1})$ for $i<n$, which is the image of $A_n$, and the second is surjective (given $(y_i)$ put $x_n=0$ and $x_i=y_i+f_i(x_{i+1})$ downwards). Kernels and cokernels of levelwise homomorphisms in the abelian category of towers [lem-pc-tower-abelian] are the levelwise ones with induced transition maps (these satisfy the universal properties levelwise), so $0\to(A_n)\to(B_n)\to(C_n)\to0$ is a short exact sequence of towers. A compatible family in $\varprojlim B_n$ is $b_n=(x_n,\dots,x_1)$ for a unique $(x_i)\in\prod_iA_i$, so $\varprojlim_nB_n=\prod_nA_n$, likewise $\varprojlim_nC_n=\prod_nA_n$, and under these identifications $\varprojlim(B_n\to C_n)$ is $(x_i)\mapsto(x_i-f_i(x_{i+1}))_i=1-s$,  A morphism of towers $(\varphi_n)$ induces $\bigoplus\varphi_i$ on $B_n,C_n$, giving a morphism of these short exact sequences compatible with all identifications.

source.place: Tag 07KW, Lemma 15.88.1, proof: the systems (B_n), (C_n) and the short exact sequence 0 -> (A_n) -> (B_n) -> (C_n) -> 0

proof.text: The towers $(B_n)$ and $(C_n)$ of the preceding construction have surjective transition maps, so $R^q\varprojlim B_n=R^q\varprojlim C_n=0$ for all $q\geq1$ by [lem-pc-tower-surjective-lim-acyclic]. The hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor] hold for $v=\varprojlim$ on towers: the tower category has enough injectives and the limit is additive by hypothesis, and the limit preserves finite limits since it is a right adjoint, and with $R^0\varprojlim=\varprojlim$ [def-sp-left-exact-additive] its part (2) gives, for the short exact sequence of the preceding construction, the exact sequence $0\to\varprojlim A_n\to\varprojlim B_n\to\varprojlim C_n\xrightarrow{\delta}R^1\varprojlim A_n\to R^1\varprojlim B_n=0$ and, for $q\geq2$, $0=R^{q-1}\varprojlim C_n\to R^q\varprojlim A_n\to R^q\varprojlim B_n=0$. With the identifications of the preceding construction the first sequence reads $0\to\varprojlim A_n\to\prod_nA_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_nA_n\to R^1\varprojlim A_n\to0$, so $\delta$ induces $\operatorname{coker}(1-s)\cong R^1\varprojlim_nA_n$; the second gives $R^q\varprojlim_nA_n=0$ for $q\geq2$. Naturality in $(A_n)$: a morphism of towers gives a morphism of the short exact sequences of the preceding construction, and the connecting maps are natural by part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor].
